title: Reserved pool cooldown miscalculation causes scale thrash and tenant request starvation
creator: Sasha Patel
description: Summary: Several high-volume tenants observed repeated coldstart spikes and 504s over a 3-hour window due to the reserved-pool cooldown computation underestimating warmup time for heterogenous instance types. The autoscaler reacted by repeatedly scaling down then back up (thrashing), which depleted burst credits and caused customer-facing timeouts. A mid-priority customer (MediData) filed an SLA escalation after a clinical workflow failed during the outage. This ticket tracks the emergency fix, customer communications, and the follow-up engineering tasks to prevent regression.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate burst traffic pattern across a mix of GPU types (A100 and T4 emulation) to a reserved pool tenant
Start with cold pool state then inject sustained 30s spike followed by 90s lull repeated 6 times
Observe autoscaler decision timeline in /internal/autoscaler/events and reserved pool cooldown calculation
Measure request latencies and 504s surfaced by routing logs for the tenant

root_cause_summary: The autoscaler's cooldown logic used a single global warmup_time constant and a linear headroom multiplier derived from homogeneous GPU benchmarks. For mixed reserved pools (A100 + T4) the effective warmup for cached kernels and KV priming is significantly longer. The estimator therefore returned a cooldown interval that was too short, allowing the controller to reclaim capacity before the tenant's traffic fully warmed the instances. When subsequent bursts arrived, the autoscaler observed high utilization again and scaled up, creating a thrash loop that consumed burst credits and caused request queuing and timeouts.
mitigation_plan: 1) Backport and deploy PR #4123 to add a temporary suspend on aggressive downscales for impacted tenant labels. 2) Deploy PR #4131 which replaces the constant warmup_time with a per-pool warmup estimator using recent kernel-priming and KV-hit latency histograms. 3) Add a decay factor and minimum cooldown bound for mixed-GPU pools. 4) Expand canary to the three highest-traffic reserved pools for 48 hours and monitor tenant-level 5xx and warmup metrics.
postmortem_followups: Implement per-tenant warmup profiling: capture first-5-min KV-hit and kernel load latencies (ENG-240112)
Add e2e integration test that replays mixed-GPU burst patterns against autoscaler simulator (ENG-240119)
Update runbooks and SLO docs to include guidance for mixed-GPU reserved pools and recommended pool composition
Coordinate with solutions engineering to reach out to impacted customers and review capacity recommendations
